newsitem.title: USA: Sun offer needs clarification - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Sun offer needs clarification - analysts.

text.p: Sun Communities Inc's decision to offer cash to shareholders of Chateau Properties Inc, a mobile home park operator it is attempting to take over, needs further clarification, analysts said Thursday.
"Until they put a dollar sign and a number out they haven't gone cash," said Burl East, managing director of EVEREN Securities Inc.
On Wednesday, Sun said it would offer a cash alternative to its existing stock-swap merger proposal, which was valued at about $390 million.

Sun president Gary Shiffman said the offer at this time is equivalent to 0.892 share of Sun stock offered per Chateau share or operating partnership (OP) unit, or about $25.87 when the letter was sent Wednesday. He said Sun is still awaiting a response from Chateau.
"Whether or how much above this we would go would be something we would determine in conjunction with Chateau," Shiffman said in a telephone interview.
Sun stock fell Thursday, with shares off 5/8 at 28-1/4 after dipping to a low for the day of 27-3/8.
"The market is in a state of limbo until they decide to qualify it," said Kevin Comer, an analyst for BT Securities.

"Sun's stock price has been hit today and I think a lot of that might be the uncertainty surrounding the Sun offer. I think Sun is going to have a difficult time recovering until there is some clarity," Comer said.

Sun's cash offer comes after Manufactured Home Communities Inc launched a $400 million hostile takeover of the company, offering $26 a share. MHC had previously offered the cash or 1.15 MHC shares for each Chateau share or OP unit, but Chateau did not respond.
Chateau could not be reached for comment, but last week said it is still considering the proposals. Shiffman said Chateau by law must respond to MHC's tender by Tuesday.

Last July, ROC Communities Inc and Chateau agreed to combine, which analysts said opened the door to additional merger proposals. At this point, it would be nearly impossible to walk away from all of the proposals, they said.

No matter which offer Chateau chooses, analysts agree a lawsuit is likely. The conflict is over which type of investor in a REIT, or real estate investment trust, is considered most important -- the common shareholder or the OP unit holder.

The board of directors of Chateau owns mainly OP units which allow for deferred taxes, making the cash offers much less attractive, and there are more OP units than common shares. But most analysts agree the board's first priority should be the common shareholder.
The MHC cash proposal is more lucrative for the common shareholder, whereas the OP unit holders would earn more with Sun's first stock-swap proposal, analysts said.
"This will decide how REITs are structured and whether OP unit holders are valued as much as shareholders," East said. "This has not been legally challenged yet."
